title: Love, Ghosts, and World Heritage
notes: Recurring detective-cast nodes (Conan, Kogoro Mouri, Ran, Inspector Megure) omitted by convention; Ayumi Yoshida is kept as a person node because her own presence at the Water God shrine and her disputed sighting are load-bearing plot facts (they hand the detectives the culprit's flight direction), not generic sidekick commentary -- Genta and Mitsuhiko are omitted as pure banter/reaction characters. case_type: attempted_murder (present-day attack on Iwao Nagakura) plus a backstory murder (Nagakura Eiji, staged as suicide) committed by the same culprit. No `event` node type: every action is a directly typed edge between the entities involved. Old case file (cases/ep348-349_love_ghosts_and_world_heritage.json) agreed on the culprit (Sakaki/'s2') but was thin: it listed only one location and reduced the entire house-swap mechanism -- the actual engine of the mystery, where Sakaki breaks into the relocated Nagakura house believing it is still the vacant Otozawa house -- to unstated background. It also asserted Eiji was 'thrown off a cliff'; the dialogue-only transcript never states a method for Eiji's death beyond 'staged as suicide' with 'no other means of escape,' so that detail is kept out here as unconfirmed rather than repeated as fact. The old file's claim that the jewels were 'hidden near the village' is sharpened here to their actual hiding place, inside the physical Otozawa house structure, which is why the jewels moved along with the house when the two homes were swapped. Ghost figure Mami-chan (Eiji's childhood friend, died of illness ten years before present) is included as a backstory_figure since the whole plot turns on characters believing they saw her; the show itself leaves the sightings ambiguous (laundry, a Brocken specter), so the encounter edge is written as a plain 'encounters' rather than asserting a supernatural fact.
